title: A prescribed ordinary marked regular cover spreads from a henselization
statement: Let $T$ be a reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme, let $t\in T$, put $H=\mathcal O_{T,t}^h$ and $T_h=\operatorname{Spec}H$, and let $Z\subset T$ be a nowhere dense closed subset [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Suppose a specified finite ordinary alteration covering $(q_i:X_i\to T_h)_i$ is given, with each $X_i$ regular Noetherian and with specified strict normal crossings boundaries $D_i$ supported exactly on $q_i^{-1}(Z\times_TT_h)$ [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exist a separated etale morphism of finite presentation $e:T'\to T$, a point $t'\in T'$ above $t$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(t)\cong\kappa(t')$, a compatible $T$-map $T_h\to T'$ taking the closed point to $t'$, such that $T'\to T$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/T$, and a finite ordinary alteration covering $(q_i':X_i'\to T')_i$ with each $X_i'$ regular Noetherian and with strict normal crossings boundaries $D_i'$ supported exactly on $(q_i')^{-1}(e^{-1}Z)$. The base changes of the family and its boundaries along $T_h\to T'$ are isomorphic to the prescribed family and boundaries, including the diagram of boundary components, their scheme-theoretic intersections and inclusions [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-residue-field]. Empty members and empty boundaries are allowed. No prime or invertibility condition is assumed.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34; III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary-alt alternative: prescribed family and boundary diagram spread to a pointed etale neighborhood.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ containing $t$. By [lem-per-ordinary-henselian-pointed-neighbourhood-limit] there is a directed system of pointed affine separated etale finite-presentation $U$-schemes $(U_a,t_a)$, with unchanged residue field, and a henselian local limit ring $H_0$. Identify $H_0$ with the specified $H$ as follows. Each pointed etale algebra, after base change to $H$, has a unique retraction selecting its prescribed point by [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. These compatible maps give a local map $H_0\to H$. The universal property of [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] gives a local map $H\to H_0$. Their composite on $H$ is the identity by that universal property, and the composite on $H_0$ is the identity on each etale algebra by uniqueness of the retractions. Thus $T_h=\lim_a U_a$, compatibly with the points and residue fields. All transition maps are affine (their sources and targets are affine) and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: The $U_a$ are reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced], and quasi-excellent Noetherian by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability]. By [lem-per-quasi-excellent-localization] the reduced local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is quasi-excellent, and [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation] makes $H$ reduced excellent Noetherian. Every finite-type scheme used below over $T_h$ or a $U_a$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Its structure map is locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], quasi-compact by finite type, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Thus it is of finite presentation in the global sense of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Any morphism between two such models is locally of finite type by clause (f) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], hence locally of finite presentation by the same Noetherian lemma. These observations verify the finiteness hypotheses of all limit lemmas below.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Let $B_c$ be the finitely many reduced irreducible components of $T_h$; finiteness and existence are [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each $B_c$ is integral and quasi-excellent Noetherian, the latter by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability]. The morphism $B_c\to T_h$ is an alteration object: it is a closed immersion, its generic point is a component generic point, and its generic residue extension is the identity. Pull back the given covering sieve to $B_c$. The categorical fibre products are the reduced dominant parts described in [lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus]; this assertion is about the underlying category, independent of its prime parameter. The category equivalence of [lem-per-alteration-site-localization] identifies the slice at $B_c$ with $\operatorname{alt}/B_c$. It also identifies the ordinary topologies: in either category the generators are exactly jointly surjective etale families and proper surjective maps, so the equivalence carries each generator to the identical underlying family. The pulled-back finite family is therefore ordinary covering on $B_c$, by the pullback axiom of [def-weil-pbc-topos]. This uses no assertion about prime-to-a-prime covering families.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-ordinary-alteration-proper-refinement] on each nonempty integral $B_c$ to the covering of Step 3. This gives an integral $P_c$ proper surjective generically finite over $B_c$, a finite open cover $P_c=\bigcup_j V_{cj}$, and maps $V_{cj}\to X_{i(c,j)}$ over $T_h$ (compose the maps into the categorical pullbacks with their projections). Form $P=\coprod_c P_c$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Then $p:P\to T_h$ is proper and surjective: properness of each composite follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and after every base change the image of a closed subset of this finite disjoint union is the finite union of closed images. Separation and finite type are checked on the finitely many summands. The $V_{cj}$ cover $P$. Each of $P$ and $V_{cj}$ is an alteration object over $T_h$: the sources are reduced, and generic points map to component generic points with finite residue extensions. An open of an integral source is integral when nonempty, with the same generic residue field. Empty opens may be omitted. This is an explicit proper/Zariski witness refining the original family.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Descend the objects $X_i,D_i$, their labelled reduced irreducible boundary components $C_{ir}$, all their intersections, and $P,V_{cj}$ by the object clause of [thm-pd-spreading-out]. Descend the finitely many inclusions and the maps $V_{cj}\to X_{i(c,j)}$ by its morphism clause, and their commuting equations by its equality clause, choosing a common upper index $a$. Empty prescribed $X_i$ are modelled by the empty scheme from the start. For each boundary intersection use the actual fibre product of the component models; descend the isomorphism to its prescribed intersection and its inverse identities by the same two clauses. Hence the complete finite marked diagram is recovered after base change. Use [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to make all boundary inclusions closed immersions, [lem-weil-pbc-descend-open-immersion-qcqs] to make $V_{cj,a}\to P_a$ open immersions, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-family-joint-surjectivity-stage] to make them a cover, and [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] to make $p_a$ proper surjective. Step 2 verifies qcqs and local finite-presentation hypotheses, and the base transitions are affine by Step 1.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Make the finitely many $X_{i,a},P_a,V_{cj,a}$ alteration objects without imposing an invertible prime on $T$. For $r=2,3$ restrict the system to the principal opens $U_a[1/r]$. Their limits are $T_h[1/r]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. The restricted bases are reduced affine Noetherian, with affine etale transitions, and quasi-excellent because $R_a[1/r]$ is a localization of the quasi-excellent coordinate ring $R_a$ of $U_a$ [lem-per-quasi-excellent-localization]; the limits $T_h[1/r]$ are reduced, and Noetherian as open subschemes of the Noetherian $T_h$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The limit objects are restrictions to opens of the alteration objects already obtained. They are still reduced finite type, and their nonempty components have exactly the old generic points lying over that open and the same finite generic residue extensions. Apply only the object conclusion of [lem-per-ind-etale-alteration-object-degree-descent], with $\ell=r$, separately on these two systems. Choose one common later index. Since $D(2)\cup D(3)=U_a$ (no prime contains both $2$ and $3$), the models are reduced everywhere. At each component generic point choose one of these opens containing its image. The alteration-object conclusion there says its image is generic in that open, hence generic in $U_a$, with finite residue extension. Finite type already holds globally. Thus all the models are alteration objects over $U_a$. Empty principal opens cause no exception.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-ind-etale-regular-coordinate-locus] to each $X_{i,a}$ with its labelled $C_{ir,a}$ and $D_{i,a}$. The map $T_h\to U_a$ is ind-etale: the neighborhood algebra is etale over $R$ and $H$ is ind-etale over $R$ by [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale], so [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] applies to its map into $H$. The projections $X_i\to X_{i,a}$ are affine locally ind-etale by base change, and $X_i$ is Noetherian. The coordinate locus therefore pulls back to the whole $X_i$, since the prescribed boundary is strict normal crossings. Its open locus is constructible on the Noetherian $X_{i,a}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to the system of model sources; it has the given $X_i$ as limit, by base changing the limiting cone, and affine transitions. At a common later stage the whole model lies in the coordinate locus. The invariance clause of the coordinate-locus lemma under the etale transitions then gives regularity and the required local coordinate equations throughout the new models, including every marked intersection and its expected local codimension.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: At the current stage let $E_i$ be the symmetric difference of $|D_{i,a}|$ and $|X_{i,a}\times_T Z|$. It is constructible (a finite Boolean combination of closed subsets), and its inverse image in $X_i$ is empty by the specified support equality. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-contained-in-constructible] to $X_{i,a}\setminus E_i$ for each $i$. At a common later index the two supports agree everywhere. All coordinate conditions persist under the etale transition by [lem-per-ind-etale-regular-coordinate-locus]. Properness persists by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]; the open witness and its covering persist by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image]. Alteration-object conclusions persist by Step 6. Fix this stage henceforth, so no further etale change can split a retained integral component.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Each $C_{ir,a}$ is regular Noetherian by Step 7, so [rem-pc-regular-normal] makes it a finite disjoint union of integral open-and-closed components. Their inverse images partition the prescribed nonempty integral $C_{ir}$ into open-and-closed subsets. Exactly one is nonempty, and its inverse image is all of $C_{ir}$. Remove from $X_{i,a}$ the closed supports of every other component, for every label $r$, obtaining $X^o_{i,a}$. Its pullback to $T_h$ is still all of $X_i$. On this open each labelled component is a nonempty open of the retained integral component, hence integral, and is closed in $X^o_{i,a}$. The coordinate equations of Step 7 restrict to this open. They give a radical effective Cartier boundary, the union of these labels, with regular intersections and the required local codimensions. Distinct nonempty labels remain distinct: two equal labels would violate the distinct-parameter condition at any point of that common component. Thus these are precisely the components required by [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Empty boundary families require no removal. The sources stay Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and the support equality restricts unchanged.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: For each witness open $V_{cj,a}$ take the inverse image $V^o_{cj,a}$ of $X^o_{i(c,j),a}$ under its leaf map. These are opens of $P_a$ and their union $P^o_a$ pulls back to all of $P$: the leaf maps over $T_h$ land in $X_i$, and the original witness opens cover $P$. Consequently the closed complement $K=P_a\setminus P^o_a$ has empty inverse image in $P$. Its image $p_a(K)$ is closed because $p_a$ is proper. This last assertion follows directly from the definition [def-weil-proper-morphism], which says $p_a$ is universally closed and therefore closed. Moreover $t_a\notin p_a(K)$. Otherwise a point of $K$ over $t_a$ would lift after the base change to the closed point of $T_h$, since $\kappa(t_a)=\kappa(t)$; equivalently apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] with the subset $K$. This contradicts the empty inverse image. Choose an affine open $W\subset U_a\setminus p_a(K)$ containing $t_a$. Then the $V^o_{cj,a}|_W$ cover $P_a|_W$, their leaf maps factor through $X^o_{i(c,j),a}|_W$, and $P_a|_W\to W$ remains proper surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. This is the proper-witness shrinking argument of ILO II 4.1.1, written out for the specified open sources.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Put $T'=W$, $X_i'=X^o_{i,a}|_W$, and use the restricted boundaries. All schemes just used as witness objects or final sources are open subschemes of alteration objects. They remain reduced; their component generic points and finite generic residue extensions are inherited from those objects. They are finite type: Noetherian open immersions are quasi-compact and hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], followed by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Thus they belong to $\operatorname{alt}/W$. The proper surjective map $P_a|_W\to W$ and its finite Zariski open cover from Step 10 are generators for the ordinary topology of [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. Their composite family is covering: pull the generated composite sieve back along $P_a|_W\to W$; it contains the covering open family, and transitivity in [def-weil-pbc-topos] gives the claim. A supersieve of a covering sieve is covering by that same transitivity axiom, since its pullback along every arrow in the smaller sieve is maximal. The leaf maps show that the generated sieve of $(X_i'\to W)_i$ contains this composite covering sieve. Hence the prescribed indexed family of final models is ordinary covering.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: The composite $e:W\to U_a\to U\to T$ is separated etale of finite presentation. Indeed the open immersions $W\to U_a$ and $U\to T$ are separated (their diagonals identify with their sources), are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and are quasi-compact by Noetherianness and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Etaleness includes local finite presentation; open immersions are separated and hence quasi-separated. The finite-presentation convention of [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] now applies, and separation and finite presentation compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. The scheme $W$ is reduced by Step 2 and open restriction. Every generic point of $W$ maps to a generic point of $T$: apply the etale comparison of [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] to $W\to T$, with $T$ as base and $T_{\mathrm{md}}=T$. It identifies $W$ with its reduced dominant part. Residue extensions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable]. Thus $e$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/T$, as requested.

source.place: Expose II proof of Proposition 4.3.3, printed pp.33--34, and III proof of Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44, ordinary alteration alternative.

proof.text: Set $t'=t_a\in W$. Its residue field is $\kappa(t)$ by Step 1. The map $T_h\to U_a$ factors through $W$: every point of the local scheme $T_h$ generalizes its closed point, and an open containing the image of that closed point contains their images. It takes the closed point to $t'$. Every removal in Step 9 and the base restriction in Step 10 has empty complement after pullback to $T_h$. The base-change isomorphisms of Step 5 therefore recover exactly the specified $X_i,D_i$, their component labels, intersections and inclusions. The final sources are regular Noetherian and their boundaries strict normal crossings by Step 9 and restriction to opens, which changes none of the local rings or defining parameter equations. Their support is precisely the inverse image of $e^{-1}Z$ by Step 8. Empty prescribed sources and empty boundaries are retained, and no prime or invertibility hypothesis has entered the conclusion.
